answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence decays across sparse boundaries rather than spreading freely. A sybil cluster may be internally dense yet connect to honest nodes through a narrow ridge; its low-conductance external cut limits escape probability and, by min-cut transitivity bounds, caps aggregate voting weight. Thus identities beyond the trust horizon, even polished as a pearl, cannot gain major influence without independent honest attestations.
